extraFacts.fact: SAE J514 and ISO 8434-2 cover 37° flared tube and hose fittings (JIC): the male 37° flare seats metal to metal against the 37° cone of the female swivel nut, and thread sizes are given by dash number, where each dash is one sixteenth of an inch (-04 is 4/16 in, or 1/4 in).

316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 austenitic stainless steel (carbon 0.03 % maximum), which is why it can be welded without carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries; it contains molybdenum for resistance to chloride pitting.
extraFacts.source: ASTM A240 / A276 chemical composition limits for UNS S31603

faqs.q: What is the JIC 37° swivel female used for?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° swivel female is a 316L stainless-steel female JIC 37° swivel hose fitting in the straight form, with a UN/UNF thread and a 37° metal-to-metal cone seat. It connects a stainless hose to a male 37° flared port or fitting; the swivel nut lets it be tightened without twisting the hose, and the body is a straight line from hose to port.

In the JIC 37° swivel female part numbers the first two-digit number is the hose dash size and the second is the port size, so IH-SS-T43-FJX-10-10 is for a 5/8" hose and a 5/8" JIC 37° female swivel (7/8-14).

faqs.q: Which sizes does the JIC 37° swivel female come in?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° swivel female size table runs from hose size -03 (3/16") to -32 (2"). Ports run from 1/4" JIC 37° female swivel to 2" JIC 37° female swivel, and every part number gives both sizes.

faqs.q: How do I choose the size of the JIC 37° swivel female?
faqs.a: Pick the hose dash size first, then the port: in the part numbers the first number is the hose dash and the second is the JIC port dash, so -08 hose to a -10 port is a different part from -08 to -08. The size table lists both.

faqs.q: What pressure rating does the JIC 37° swivel female have?
faqs.a: The listing gives the JIC 37° swivel female no pressure figure of its own: the pressure of the finished assembly tracks the hose grade and ferrule when it is crimped to the correct diameter. Pick the hose first, then confirm that the hose rating suits the JIC 37° UN/UNF (7/16-20 to 1-7/8-12) port before you order.

faqs.q: What is the JIC 37° swivel female made from, and where does stainless suit it?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° swivel female is machined from 316L stainless steel, passivated with no plating, so its corrosion resistance comes from the native oxide layer. It suits marine, chemical, food-grade and washdown service where zinc-plated carbon steel corrodes. The listing gives -40°C to +200°C, limited by the hose and any O-ring.

faqs.q: Which standards does the JIC 37° swivel female follow?
faqs.a: The JIC 37° swivel female is listed to SAE J514 and ISO 8434-2. Both cover the 37° flare: the male flare seats metal to metal in the female nut, so the cone makes the seal, not the thread.

faqs.q: What does the JIC 37° swivel female connect to?
faqs.a: The female swivel nut of the JIC 37° swivel female screws onto a male JIC 37° end, such as the [Male JIC 37°](/p/male-jic-37). The hose side takes an SS316L crimp ferrule; see our [stainless crimp hose fittings](/c/stainless-crimp-hose-fittings).

faqs.q: How tight should the JIC 37° swivel female nut be run down?
faqs.a: Run the nut on by hand until the flare seats, then tighten it a set number of flats past finger-tight while holding the body, so the hose is not twisted. Stainless JIC threads gall, so lubricate lightly and never use thread tape on the cone.
